scope: CIFAR-10 direct/TET six-timestep VGG-9 greatest-excess non-winner regularization calibration

recipe.dynamics: beta=0.5, ATan surrogate, immediate reset, AdamW cosine schedule, norm-5 gradient clipping

three_way_lambda_0.1_comparison.interpretation: At the common coefficient lambda=0.1, exempting the greatest-excess winner preserves the no-regularization accuracy while reducing pre-pool and non-winner activity by about one quarter. Ordinary regularization yields a slightly larger activity reduction but loses 0.80 percentage points. Its unweighted penalty is 2.70 times the selective penalty at the same lambda, so a penalty-matched ordinary baseline would be a useful follow-up.

conclusion: All one-seed runs completed with active deep and output layers. Strong selective penalties reduce non-winner firing but hurt accuracy. At lambda=0.1, selective non-winner regularization is the promising fixed-strength formulation: it matched the no-regularization accuracy within 0.02 percentage points while reducing measured pre-pool activity by 24.97% and non-winner activity by 25.53%. Ordinary all-spike regularization at the same coefficient reduced activity slightly more but lost 0.80 percentage points. These are one-seed results, so the fixed-lambda comparison needs a five-seed confirmation before a statistical claim.
